extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians writing research papers (graduate students through senior researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Advice for composing, polishing, and submitting research papers in mathematics, covering macro-structure, organization, drafting, polishing, reading skills, career-stage goals, and submission etiquette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the introduction to "sell" the key points
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the introduction to 'sell' the key points. State results in appropriate detail; consider stating a special case before the general theorem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the introduction present the results clearly and attractively; give statements with the right level of detail and possibly present a simple special case first to convey ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't write a paper until your work is mature
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't write a paper until your work is mature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid premature publication which wastes readers' time; ensure results and structure are stable before composing the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite generously
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite generously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include not only direct sources but adjacent/contextual work to situate the result; acknowledge intellectual debts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create lemmas
rubrics_metrics.description: Create lemmas. Break the paper into modular pieces; each piece does one thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modularization makes proofs easier to read and reuse; isolate technical steps into lemmas so the main thread is clearer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose good notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose good notation. Mnemonic, consistent, sparse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notation choice often dictates whether the proof reads cleanly; treat notation as a design decision and invest time in it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write in your own voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Write in your own voice. Don't mimic; develop personal style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize clarity over imitation; cultivate a writing voice that communicates ideas effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take advantage of the English language
rubrics_metrics.description: Take advantage of the English language. Use prose where prose is clearer than symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: English carries connotation that pure formula does not; prefer words when they make the exposition clearer rather than excessive symbolic notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid prototype the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Rapid prototype the paper. A complete bad first draft is better than half a polished one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce a full initial draft quickly to reveal structure and gaps; iteration beats partial perfection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't over-optimize early sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't over-optimize early sections. Wait until the whole structure is stable before polishing prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defer heavy polishing until the paper's organization and arguments are settled to avoid wasted effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate the bored, hostile, and confused reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate the bored reader, the hostile reader, and the confused reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-empt common objections and difficulties by clarifying motivation, addressing likely criticisms, and filling gaps that would confuse readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be considerate of your audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Be considerate of your audience. What does your reader already know? What will they need?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust level of detail, background, and notation to the intended readership; write for the most distant potential reader among those you expect.

rubrics_metrics.name: State main results in appropriate detail
rubrics_metrics.description: State main results in appropriate detail. Restate after the proof if the result is hidden inside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure theorems are stated precisely and accessibly; if proofs obscure the statement, restate conclusions clearly for the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a roadmap section in long papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a roadmap section in long papers explaining the global proof structure before the technical details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For long, technical papers, give a global overview of the argument to orient readers before diving into details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofread thoroughly
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofread thoroughly. Multiple passes; ideally several days apart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do many careful readings with time gaps to catch errors, improve clarity, and refine exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose the right journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose the right journal. Match scope, prestige, and audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a venue appropriate to the paper's topic, technical level, and intended readership rather than only prestige.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to referee reports point-by-point
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to referee reports point-by-point. Acknowledge every comment, even minor ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When revising, address each referee remark explicitly to show you have considered and acted on feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify 'compilation errors' when reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying 'compilation errors' — sentences that don't parse logically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a reader or reviser, look for sentences that are grammatically or logically malformed; these should be fixed to improve clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize implicit notational conventions from context
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing implicit notational conventions from context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be attentive to notation that the author expects the reader to infer; as an author, make conventions clear to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locate the 'jumps in difficulty'
rubrics_metrics.description: Locating the 'jumps in difficulty' — where the author has skipped real work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect places where nontrivial steps are elided; fill or signpost such gaps for readers, or provide references/lemmas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish local from global errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguishing local from global errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When revising, separate small wording/notation fixes from structural or conceptual issues that affect the whole paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-PhD stage writing advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-PhD: copy structure of mentor's papers; focus on correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At an early stage, learn by emulating advisors' papers and prioritize getting correct, complete results rather than stylistic polish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early postdoc stage writing advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Early postdoc: polish prose; develop voice; work on introduction-craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin to refine exposition, form a personal style, and learn to write effective introductions that motivate and explain results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mid-career stage writing advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Mid-career: write expository/survey pieces; teach the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contribute broader exposition and syntheses that help communicate the field to others; focus on clarity and pedagogy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior stage writing advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior: aim for definitive treatments and books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce comprehensive, authoritative accounts of topics; consolidate knowledge and set a high standard for exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity above brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity above brevity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer being clear over being terse; avoid sacrificing understanding for compactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation before formality
rubrics_metrics.description: Motivation before formality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the ideas and reasons for a result before presenting the formal statement and proof to help readers grasp significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: English over symbols when both work
rubrics_metrics.description: English over symbols when both work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a sentence can be more clearly stated in words rather than symbols, use prose to convey nuance and intuition.

rubrics_metrics.name: State the theorem precisely before proving
rubrics_metrics.description: State the theorem precisely before proving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give exact statements so readers know what is being proved; avoid hiding the precise claim inside the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write the introduction last
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the introduction last.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose the introduction after the body so it accurately summarizes and 'sells' what the paper actually contains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation is design; spend real time on it
rubrics_metrics.description: Notation is design; spend real time on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat notation choices deliberately as part of exposition design; good notation reduces reader confusion and cognitive load.

rubrics_metrics.name: A paper has many readers; write for the most distant
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper has many readers; write for the most distant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider varied audiences (experts, non-experts, future readers) and aim for accessibility to those less familiar with specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge intellectual debts
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge intellectual debts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give credit to prior work and influences through citations and explicit acknowledgments; this is part of good scholarly practice.
